title: K-IR v0.1 Proposition
description: Formal schema for a single canonical K-IR proposition atom, derived directly from failure cases already found in the physics and ML/AI benchmarks (causal-kg-benchmark and ml-ai-dataset/benchmark). Deliberately does NOT include GENERALIZES_METHOD, COMPOSES_TO, causal-edge types, or an ontology beyond what a handful of examples force -- per the decision to derive the relation algebra from real failures, not design it upfront. See STRESS_TEST.md for where this schema already breaks on the 12 hand-compiled examples.

predicate.description: Symbolic relation name. Deliberately a small, fixed core rather than one predicate per concept: MONOTONIC (paired with 'direction'), EQUALS (for defining/algebraic identities), SUBTYPE_OF (ontology), IMPLIES_STATE (state x -> state y, e.g. Boiling), DISJOINT (two types/regimes cannot co-occur), MASKS (for dropout/dropconnect-style zeroing mechanisms), HOLDS (generic fact holding under context, catch-all for claims that don't fit the others -- expected to be the first thing that needs splitting once more examples arrive).

role.description: e.g. 'input', 'output', 'subject', 'object', 'target'. Which argument slot of `predicate` this fills.

direction.description: Only meaningful when predicate=MONOTONIC. A property of the RELATION (increasing vs decreasing), not of the whole proposition's truth value -- kept separate from `polarity` for exactly that reason.

type.description: The type the variable ranges over, e.g. 'Copper', 'Metal', 'Water'. This is where specialization/generalization structurally lives (Copper vs Metal), NOT in context.entity_type -- see STRESS_TEST.md item 1 for why this split is already shaky.

polarity.description: Whether the proposition as a whole is being asserted or its negation is. Kept separate from `direction` (which is about the relation's shape, e.g. increasing vs decreasing) and from `modality` (which is about how strongly/universally it's being asserted).

modality.description: universal = no exceptions permitted by construction; generic/typical = true of ordinary/unexceptional members of the quantified type, admits named exceptions (e.g. 'metals expand when heated' is generic -- Invar is a real exception); possible = can occur, not claimed to always occur; necessary = reserved for logical/mathematical necessity (definitional identities like Ohm's law within its stated regime).

surface_forms.description: Natural-language / equation / code paraphrases that compile to this atom. Optional but expected in practice for canonicalization testing.

notes.description: Known simplifications or caveats, same convention as the physics/ML benchmarks' scope_note/notes fields.

Term.description: A first-order term: a variable, a constant, or a function applied to terms.

Context.description: Structured conditions under which the proposition holds. CRITICAL RULE (derived from the BatchNorm ORIG/REVISED case): context must only encode conditions in the WORLD the proposition is about (physical regime, training/inference phase, value ranges). It must NEVER encode when a claim was published, which paper made it, or the state of scientific consensus at a point in time -- that belongs in `provenance`, not `context`. Conflating the two turns a genuine contradiction between two claimed mechanisms into a fake COMPATIBLE-via-different-era split, which is exactly the failure mode this benchmark's BN_ORIG/BN_REVISED pair exists to catch.

entity_type.description: Additional type/category restrictions beyond the quantified variable's own type. Overlaps with quantification[].type in ways not yet resolved -- see STRESS_TEST.md item 1.

temporal_domain.description: Genuine real-world time/sequencing (e.g. 'before ignition'), NEVER publication chronology or belief-revision history. See Context-level description.

value_domain.description: Numeric/ordinal range constraints on a term appearing in the proposition, e.g. Temperature(x) in [4, boiling_point(x)).

assumptions.description: Free-text background conditions not otherwise structured, e.g. 'constant_pressure', 'no_phase_transition', 'fixed_mass'. Expected to be the pressure-release valve for everything the structured fields above don't capture -- see STRESS_TEST.md item 4.
